_comment: Site-specific configuration for the https://dropbox.com replica.
The pipeline scripts are URL-agnostic; everything site-specific lives here.
_captureMode: 'rendered' is required for this site, and the evidence is unusually clear.
The pre-JS server response (index.static.html) is 91% of the elements and
94% of the asset nodes, so 'auto' picked 'static' — but what it is missing is
exactly the content that matters:
1. The security testimonial grid ([class*=quoteCardsGrid]) is present in
static but with children=0 — i.e. a VISIBLE EMPTY HOLE. Rendered has 3
cards, 3 images and 497 chars of quote text. Confirmed at DOM level, not
by substring count.
2. All 4 autoplay product videos are absent from static, which ships PNG
stills in their place (the site upgrades them client-side).
The usual objection to 'rendered' — baked runtime clones — does NOT apply
here: a DOM-level duplicate-heading census returns the SAME 3 duplicates for
both sources ('Teams', 'Use cases', 'Industries', which are genuine nav
dropdown labels appearing in both desktop and mobile menus). Rendered's only
contamination is 3 body-level iframes, all droppable by selector below.
Known, accepted consequence: the rendered capture caught the Cloudflare A/B
variant headline ('One place to store, share, and finish the job'); the static
control reads 'Find, organize, and share your work, all in one place'. The
live page serves either at random, so an h1 mismatch in `npm run compare` is
expected noise, not a defect.

_skipStylesheets: Cascade position 4 of the <head> links font_sharp_grotesk-vflwgPRUu.scss —
and Dropbox serves the raw, UNCOMPILED SCSS SOURCE at that URL: it still
contains `// comments` and `$font_weight_book: 400` declarations, and all
15 of its @font-face src url()s are unresolved SCSS interpolations.
A browser just applies CSS error recovery and drops the lot, which is why
the capture's network log shows ZERO font requests from this sheet. But
webpack's postcss parses eagerly and hard-fails: 'Unknown word (5:4)' at
the first `//`, which fails `next build` outright.
Safe to skip, on two verified grounds:
1. It is the ONLY sheet of all 123 with unmapped /static/ url()s (75 of
them); every other sheet is fully localized to /assets.
position 15, i.e. LATER and therefore winning) is the compiled build
of the very same source: identical 15 @font-face rules, the identical
numeric font-weights 400/500/600, and all 75 url()s self-hosted.
vendor-04 defines no selector rules at all — only @font-face.

_quicktimeNote: Each of the 4 videos declares three <source>s in this order:
The capture browser's network log proves Chromium fetched ONLY the 4 .webm
(HTTP 206) and issued ZERO requests for any .mov. The scraper still pulled
the .mov files from markup, and the hero one alone is 141MB (~155MB total,
far larger than the rest of the replica combined) for bytes no audited
browser ever loads. So the quicktime <source> is dropped and those 4 files
are deleted. Deviation from live: Safari would fall back to the webm's
transparency support rather than hvc1. Nothing the 7-viewport Chromium gate
or the pixel diff can observe.
_extraAssets: The page declares <link rel="shortcut icon"> pointing at the CDN copy of
favicon.ico, but the capture browser never requested it (it had the icon
cached), so scrape never downloaded it and codegen dropped the icon link
rather than leak a remote request. Naming it here downloads it, which both
restores the declared icon AND gives fetch-extras a real .ico to copy to
public/favicon.ico — Chromium probes the origin root for that unconditionally
from the browser process, and the resulting 404 is invisible to Playwright's
request events while still tripping the console-error gate.
